figures.finding: A resident pays IRPP under a family quotient: annual taxable pay less a 20% allowance is divided by family shares (Q), taxed at 0% to XAF 1,500,000 and then 5% to 35% (above 11 million) by the bracket formulas, times the shares; plus the complementary salary tax (TCTS) of 5% on pay above XAF 150,000 a month.

value.quotientFormula: Q = (12 x monthly gross - 20% allowance) / shares

figures.applies: Persons taxable in Gabon, calendar year 2026.

sources.said: Q = [(S x 12) - A] / P (as Q is annual) P = Family quotient (number of shares). S = Monthly taxable gross income. A = 20% allowance.
The TCTS rate is 5% of the salary, indemnities, and emoluments paid to the taxpayer. The part of the revenue up to XAF 150,000 per month is exempted from the TCTS.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the individual return is due before 1 March 2027.

sources.said: The tax year is the calendar year in Gabon.
The counterfoil of the individual forms is given to the employees for their personal tax return, which must be filed before 1 March of each year.

figures.finding: The employer withholds IRPP and TCTS monthly and pays them to the Treasury before the 15th of the following month.

sources.said: The IRPP and the TCTS are withheld monthly by the employer and paid over (before the 15th day of the following month) to the Public Treasury.

figures.finding: The employee pays 2.5% CNSS and 2% CNAMGS health; the employer 20.1% (family 8%, retirement 5%, injury 3%, health 4.1%); the base is capped at XAF 1.5 million a month.

sources.said: However, there is an annual ceiling of XAF 18 million (or XAF 1.5 million per month).
The employees pay 2.5% for the CNSS and 2% for the National Disease Insurance and Social Guarantee Fund (CNAMGS). The other social security contributions represent 20.1% of the taxable salary.

figures.finding: A fee paid from Gabon to a person without a permanent base there, for an independent profession practised or services used in Gabon, bears a 25% withholding, as do copyright payments.

value.base: independent professions, services rendered or used in Gabon, copyrights

figures.applies: Non-residents without a permanent professional base in Gabon.

sources.said: All amounts paid pursuant to the practice of an 'independent profession' in Gabon. Payments received by inventors, payments relating to copyrights, and all payments relating to intellectual and commercial property as well as assimilated rights. All amounts paid for services materially rendered or effectively used in Gabon.

figures.finding: A freelancer becomes liable to VAT once turnover reaches XAF 60 million; the standard rate is 18%.

sources.said: The aforesaid persons, subject to CIT or personal income tax (PIT), being registered or not, are liable to VAT should their turnover out of taxes reach XAF 60 million.
The standard VAT rate in Gabon is 18%, which applies to all transactions unless otherwise provided for by the law.
